corrections.caveats: Benchmark code is in the repo (pkg/decode, pkg/encode, pkg/stream tests; baseline wrappers in pkg/util/varint.go call encoding/binary Uvarint/PutUvarint) and the README table matches go test output, but the Go version is not stated (go.mod says go 1.16) and the machine is a single macOS i7-8700B. Microbenchmarks on 8 values plus streamed counts. The slow side is Go's own scalar LEB128 varint; the repo's own scalar Stream VByte path (about 1659 MB/s decode) already beats it, so much of the gain is the format, not only SIMD. Encode-side streaming is less impressive: WriteAllFast/Count_1e6 3218.21 MB/s vs WriteAllVarint 1735.08 MB/s (about 1.9x, derived from page data). No comparison to the C reference or other Go SIMD codecs. x86_64 AVX/AVX2 only for the fast path. Last commit 2021-09-12.

notes: All claimed numbers found verbatim in the README benchmark block. Metadata checked on github.com: Apache-2.0, 18 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2021-09-12 (abandoned, >3 years).

Author-run, bench code public (zig build bench -Doptimize=ReleaseFast) but the Zig version and CPU model are not printed in the result file (CPU only from file name), so C.

corrections.workload: Compress and decompress synthetic u8 to u128 arrays (datasets width7, width15, width32, width33 in plain, delta_ and frame_ variants; lengths 10, 69, 1023, 1024, 1025, 123321, 262144, 263167) with FastLanes-based bitpacking, versus lz4, zstd(level 1) and memcopy.
corrections.caveats: Compares against general-purpose lz4 and zstd, not against varint, Simple8b or FastPFor, so it does not show a win over the category's integer-codec baselines. Synthetic data. CPU model and Zig version come from the file name and build.zig.zon, not the result file. Lengths that are not a multiple of 1024 take a slow path: at u32 width7 LENGTH=1023 zint_bitpack decompresses at 3.709GB/s vs 8.359GB/s for memcopy and at u8 width7 LENGTH=1023 at 0.776GB/s vs lz4 5.042GB/s; at lengths 10 and 69 it is slower than lz4 and memcopy. zint_deltapack on non-delta data expands (ratio=103). The epyc results were committed on 2025-12-21, the day before the AVX-512 optimization commit, so they may not reflect HEAD. Author's own benchmark; zint_bitpack beating memcopy reflects throughput reported per uncompressed byte while touching about 21% of the bytes.
